title: Development and validation of a nitrogen dioxide passive sampler
author: Hasannezhad Estiri, Rahmani Sani, et al.

steps.title: Prepare stainless steel filters
steps.instruction: Immerse three stainless‑steel filters in 25 mL triethanolamine + 25 mL acetone for 20 min, then dry them in a controlled environment.

steps.title: Assemble passive sampler
steps.instruction: Place the dried filters at the closed end of a polyethylene diffusion tube (7.1 cm long, 1 cm diameter) and seal with a specialized lid; leave the opposite end open for air intake, install three such tubes per sampler, and house the samplers in a shelter that blocks direct sunlight and weather.

steps.title: Gather passive sampling materials
steps.instruction: Collect the following items: polyethylene diffusion tubes (7.1 cm × 1 cm), still‑filters (mesh 150 µm, 1 cm diameter), distilled water, sulfanilamide, orthophosphoric acid, N‑(1‑naphthyl)ethylenediamine dihydrochloride (NEDA), ethanolamine, acetone; all reagents are laboratory‑grade from Merck, Germany.

steps.title: Extract passive filters and react
steps.instruction: Remove each filter from its tube into an individual test tube, add 4 mL of a 1:1 mixture of reagent 1 and reagent 2, shake on a shaker for 30 min, then measure the absorbance at 510 nm with a DR5000 spectrophotometer.

substeps.instruction: Absorbent solution: dissolve 4 g NaOH in distilled water, add 1 g sodium arsenite, and bring to 1000 mL in a volumetric flask.
Sulfanilamide solution: dissolve 20 g sulfanilamide in 700 mL distilled water, add 50 mL 85 % phosphoric acid while stirring, then bring to 1000 mL; store refrigerated ≤1 month.
NEDA solution: dissolve 0.5 g NEDA in 500 mL distilled water; store refrigerated ≤1 month protected from light.
Hydrogen‑peroxide solution: dilute 2.0 mL 30 % H₂O₂ in 250 mL distilled water; store refrigerated ≤1 month protected from light.

steps.title: Calibrate SKC sampling pump
steps.instruction: Connect two standard‑nozzle impingers and one fritted‑nozzle impinger in series (each containing 10 mL absorbent solution), use a soap‑bubble set to adjust the pump flow to 142 mL min⁻¹, employing the bypass valve as needed.

steps.title: Collect active air sample
steps.instruction: Attach the calibrated pump (flow = 142 mL min⁻¹) to the three impingers, sample ambient air for 24 h at 2 m height, then transfer the combined absorbent solution into a graduated vial and store at 4 °C until analysis.

steps.title: Analyze active samples colorimetrically
steps.instruction: Correct any evaporation loss by adding distilled water, mix, then:

substeps.instruction: Aliquot 10 mL of the sample into a 50 mL volumetric flask.
Add 1 mL hydrogen‑peroxide solution, 10 mL sulfanilamide solution, and 4.1 mL NEDA solution.
Fill to the 50 mL mark with distilled water and mix.
Measure absorbance at 510 nm using the DR5000 spectrophotometer.
Prepare a control by processing 10 mL of unexposed absorbent solution identically.

steps.title: Convert sampled volume to STP
steps.instruction: Calculate the standard‑temperature‑pressure volume (Vr) using Vr = (V × P / 101.3) × (298.15 / T), where V is the collected air volume (L), P the average atmospheric pressure (kPa), and T the average temperature (K) at the sampling site.

steps.title: Calculate NO₂ concentration
steps.instruction: Compute NO₂ concentration with C = (A × m × 10³ × v) / Vr, where A is the measured absorbance, m the calibration factor (µg NO₂ · mL⁻¹ · abs⁻¹), v the volume of absorbent solution used in the colour reaction (mL), and Vr the STP‑adjusted air volume (L).

description: This stud was conducted in Sabzevar, Iran (2022). We developed a simple passive sampler to measure ambient NO2 in urban areas. The performance of the developed passive sampler was evaluated by comparing it with a standard method for measuring NO2 [1].
